findings.problem: TelemetryWorkflow uses primitive fields (status: String, is_validated: bool, is_sent: bool, sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64>) that allow impossible state combinations: e.g. is_sent=true with status="pending", or sent_at_epoch_ms=Some(100) with is_sent=false. The struct has no constructor enforcing lifecycle invariants.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct any bit-pattern of fields including invalid lifecycle transitions, making it impossible to reason about the state machine at compile time.
findings.fix: Replace status with an enum (e.g. TelemetryStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent }) and is_sent/sent_at_epoch_ms into a typestate or single timestamp field. Remove is_sent boolean (redundant with Sent variant). Replace is_validated bool with a typestate step or validated_at_epoch_ms.

findings.problem: All fields of TelemetryWorkflow are pub on raw primitives (String, bool, Option). There is no parse boundary or smart constructor to reject invalid values at the module boundary.
findings.failure_mode: Callers can construct invalid states directly (e.g. id="", status="foo", is_sent=true) without any validation.
findings.fix: Parse at the boundary into newtypes and enum variants through fallible constructors. Use impl TelemetryWorkflow { fn new(...) -> Result<Self, TelemetryError> } that rejects invalid combinations.

findings.problem: status: String is a primitive string, not a domain enum. mark_sent does item.status = "sent".to_string() which allocates a new String every call.
findings.failure_mode: Status values are not enforced by the type system. Typos or unexpected strings create silent bugs. String allocation on every state transition adds unnecessary heap pressure.
findings.fix: Replace with enum TelemetryStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent } and mark_sent sets item.status = TelemetryStatus::Sent (no allocation).

findings.problem: item.status = "sent".to_string() performs a heap allocation on every call. mark_sent is a state transition that should be a simple field assignment.
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocation on every state transition. If called in a hot loop or high-throughput path, this creates allocator pressure and potential allocation failures.
findings.fix: Replace status String with an enum so mark_sent uses a zero-cost assignment: item.status = TelemetryStatus::Sent.

findings.problem: is_sent: bool and sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> are redundant with status: String. When status is "sent", is_sent must be true and sent_at_epoch_ms must be Some. This is information duplication that creates inconsistency risk.
findings.failure_mode: State inconsistencies: is_sent=true with sent_at_epoch_ms=None, or is_sent=false with status="sent".
findings.fix: Use a single enum with associated data: enum TelemetryStatus { Pending, Validated, Sent { sent_at_epoch_ms: u64 } }. This makes it a compile error to have Sent without a timestamp.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain semantics. Any String can be used as an id.
findings.failure_mode: Domain logic can mix up IDs with other strings. No validation that id is non-empty or well-formed.
findings.fix: Replace with newtype struct TelemetryId(String) with a fallible constructor that validates non-emptiness.

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for mark_sent or any performance claim. The .to_string() allocation on every call is unmeasured.
findings.failure_mode: Unknown whether the allocation is acceptable for the workload. Without benchmarks, performance cannot be verified or optimized.
findings.fix: Add a microbenchmark for mark_sent measuring allocation count (using criterion or similar). If throughput is critical, eliminate the allocation by using an enum status.

findings.problem: No profiler evidence exists to show where time is spent in mark_sent or the broader telemetry pipeline.
findings.failure_mode: Cannot confirm whether mark_sent is a hot path or a bottleneck. Performance optimization decisions are ungrounded.
findings.fix: Run flamegraph or perf on a representative workload to identify hot paths before optimizing.

missing_evidence: no benchmark for mark_sent allocation behavior
no profiler data for telemetry pipeline hot paths
no allocation audit (no --cap-lints warn or alloc-count instrumentation)
no command evidence for cargo fmt, cargo clippy, or cargo test
residual_risk: The crate has fundamental type-level violations that prevent the compiler from enforcing domain invariants. Without enum-based status and typestate design, any consumer can construct invalid telemetry states. Performance impact of String allocation on every state transition is unmeasured. Static review only; no commands run.
